papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies an additive nuclear-norm correction after each optimizer step. In 124M–500M LLaMA experiments, it lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss. At 500M and a 4% distortion budget, the reported compression is 1.89× versus 1.14× with standard weight decay.
papers.relevance: The closest match to training for low-rank compressibility, spectral regularization, and generalization under label noise.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with 124 124 M to 500 500 M parameters, spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
For the 500 500 M model and a 4 % 4\% distortion budget, it supports 1.89 × 1.89\times compression, compared with 1.14 × 1.14\times after standard weight decay.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: BMuon modifies Muon’s geometry to favor structured MLP-channel pruning. In a 1B LLaMA-style model, it retains nearly its unpruned perplexity after 80% channel pruning, but its unpruned perplexity is worse than Muon’s.
papers.relevance: Tests whether optimizer geometry can improve compressibility and makes the dense-quality trade-off explicit.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning.
BMuon preserves its unpruned performance up to 80 % 80\% pruning, reaching 12.86 12.86 with activation ranking and 12.85 12.85 with μ \mu ranking.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Develops singular-mode birth, saturation, and decay laws for several optimizer geometries in balanced, aligned matrix-factorization models. Controlled matrix-factorization and regression experiments test the predicted dynamics.
papers.relevance: Provides a theoretical lens for how optimizer choice changes spectra and transient low-rank bias.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.
Controlled experiments in deep matrix factorization and regression verify the derived phase laws.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: ORCA applies temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in pretraining. With a shared 50k-step budget and the same learning-rate tuning protocol, its reported validation loss is 2.8106, versus 2.8460 for Muon and 2.8824 for Adam in the cited setting.
papers.relevance: Directly probes whether temporary spectral shaping improves LLM optimization without permanently constraining weight spectra.

evidence.quote: All trials share the same data, batch size, sequence length, and 50k-step training budget.
All four optimizers use this protocol and the same tuning budget.
with final validation losses of 2.8824 2.8824 , 2.8460 2.8460 , 2.9790 2.9790 , and 2.8106 2.8106 , respectively

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting low-rank gradient subspaces during LLM training. At rank 16 on a 130M model, it reports validation perplexity of 43.61 versus 60.29 for GaLore. In separate 1B measurements at rank 32, optimizer-step peak memory is 0.2487 GB versus GaLore’s 0.3385 GB.
papers.relevance: A direct GaLore-style alternative for studying quality, rank, memory, and time trade-offs.

evidence.quote: when training the 130M model at an aggressively low rank of just 16, Ori achieves a validation perplexity of 43.61, substantially outperforming GaLore (60.29) and OSD (54.05).
at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Monarch–Muon trains structured weight factors and reduces the cost of Muon updates. On one H100 at a 6.89B dense-reference size, reported peak memory falls from 68.87 to 52.94 GB and full-step time from 2986.9 to 1638.6 ms relative to dense Muon. The systems measurements are separate from complete quality runs.
papers.relevance: Addresses training memory and throughput across model scales, including a small-model crossover where the structure does not help.

evidence.quote: At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: A module-matched LoRA rank sweep examines generalization under label noise. On Qwen2.5-7B classification with 20% noisy labels, every sampled LoRA rank, including parameter parity, has higher test NLL than dense fine-tuning of the same projections across three paired seeds.
papers.relevance: Connects adapter rank, noisy-label memorization, and practical language-model fine-tuning with explicit controls.

evidence.quote: Every sampled rank, parity included, remains behind dense in all three seeds
Seeds control the subset, the noise draw, the head init and the adapter init, and are shared across arms, so the differences below are paired.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: Defines a LoRA adapter’s behavioral rate as the serialized size needed to retain a specified fraction of held-out fine-tuning gain. The paper reports receiver-dependent compressibility and, in one corrupted-data experiment, GSM8K accuracy rising from 23.7% after fine-tuning to 82.9% after compression, against 77.6% for the frozen model.
papers.relevance: Challenges rank and weight-reconstruction error as proxies for useful adapter information and links compression to noisy-data behavior.

evidence.quote: the same datasets can require substantially different rates across frozen models, with their ordering changing across receivers.
On Qwen2.5-7B, for example, GSM8K accuracy falls from 77.6% to 23.7% after corrupted fine-tuning and returns to 82.9% after compression.

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: RoM uses the gauge symmetry of LoRA factorization to optimize on a fixed-rank manifold. In Qwen2.5-3B GRPO fine-tuning at rank 16, it reports MATH-500 accuracy of 64.9% versus Adam’s 62.9%, with 1.08× end-to-end time per optimizer step.
papers.relevance: Adds direct evidence on LoRA factorization geometry and the practical cost and benefit of a gauge-aware optimizer.

evidence.quote: We design our optimizer on the manifold of fixed-rank matrices, aiming to optimize the product of the low-rank factors directly rather than each factor separately.

papers.title: Rotated Manifold Optimization for Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Idea2Prior combines discovery, identity checks, abstract assessment, citation expansion, and bounded PDF evidence to rank papers from research ideas. Its historical comparison reports 53.3% Hit@5 overall, while noting a HARD-tier exception and limits of designated-target evaluation.
papers.relevance: Directly informs paper retrieval, evidence inspection, and evaluation design for the research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: It combines multi-source discovery, identity verification, facet-based abstract assessment, semantic citation expansion, and joint Expert ranking.
A designated-target miss can coexist with useful related papers, so target Hit@5 should be complemented by independently adjudicated relevance and usefulness.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: The cited results are reported by the papers; no independent replication or code execution was performed.
Ori’s quoted memory measure is optimizer-step peak memory, not total training peak memory.
Monarch–Muon’s large-model systems measurements are separate from its complete quality runs.
The matrix-factorization analysis does not establish that its phase laws transfer to LLM pretraining.
The retrieved passages do not quantify spectral weight decay’s training overhead or RoM’s peak-memory cost.
Idea2Prior’s comparison is historical and uses a released benchmark, not an independently adjudicated paper-usefulness evaluation.
